title: Generative AI, Microdramas to Take Center Stage at Busan Market
description:
The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the Busan International Film Festival‘s (BIFF) official market, has finalized its 2026 lineup.

	InnoAsia,
body:
The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the Busan International Film Festival‘s (BIFF) official market, has finalized its 2026 lineup.

	InnoAsia, drawing 44 organizations and companies into 11 programs, leads with a deep push into generative AI and emerging media formats. ACFM has teamed with Kling AI for “New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI,” paired with a dedicated networking reception for the AI firm. Additional sessions include “Making What’s Next: Generative AI and the Future of Filmmaking at Eyeline,” “InnoAsia Cinematic AI,” “InnoAsia AI Creators Camp” and “InnoAsia Next Foundation.” 
	

	Two further sessions, “InnoAsia The Evolution of Microdrama: China & Beyond” and “Rags 2 Richmond: From Viral Microdrama to Feature Film, and the Future of Trans-Media IP,” zero in on microdrama’s rise. The “InnoAsia WIP Showcase” rounds up 11 in-progress works, among them projects from director Kang Yunsung and Climax Studio, and “Cinema by Brand” spotlights three brand-and-film collaborations chosen through an open call.


	Seven sections make up the wider lineup – The A, Asian Project Market (APM), Busan Story Market (Bsm), InnoAsia, Producer Hub, Doc Square and Platform Busan – spread across eight venues over the four-day run.

	Thailand takes on the newly created role of Country of Honor, bringing five genre features to “BSM Pitch & Match – Thai Remake IP,” a strand within BSM’s freshly launched Remake IP category. A companion initiative, “Thailand: The Next Chapter,” aims to link Thai talent with investors and audiences beyond the region.
	

	Japan holds this edition’s Focus Country designation under Producer Hub, where 10 Japanese producers will pitch their projects in “Focusing on Japan: Pitch Showcase of 10 Selected Producers,” organized alongside Vipo. That kicks off a broader 12-program Producer Hub slate touching on how streaming and short-form platforms are reshaping the business, with producers spanning Korea, Indonesia, Japan, Taiwan and beyond comparing notes, a Brazil-Korea co-production model on the agenda, and a first-time “Morning Networking” session added to the schedule.

	The A section turns its focus to distribution and capital. “The A Summit: AFAN Spotlight – The Dynamic Shifts and Shake-up for Film Distribution in Asia” gathers regional distribution figures to weigh how the business is changing, while “The A Summit: Investor Summit & Connect” digs into co-production trends and where film financing is headed.

	Doc Square’s 10-program docket centers on Oct. 12’s “Impact Asia Impact Day,” built around the social reach of Asian documentaries, with sessions on Korea, Taiwan and Japan drawing on case studies such as the Taiwanese film “Small Talk” and the Japanese film “What Should We Have Done?”

	Platform Busan opens each of the four mornings with “Platform Busan Pitch & Meet” and rounds out its slate with “Film Festivals & Markets 101,” “Becoming Punk: An International Co-production Case Study of ‘Ria'” featuring producer Christine de Leon, “An Introduction to TorinoFilmLab,” “EFM × ACFM: Connecting Berlin and Busan,” “Connecting Asia & Ibero-America: Unlocking Market Opportunities in Co-Production and Distribution” and “Uta × Gold House: Hollywood & The Asian Diaspora.” The market’s programming also includes the ACFM Awards Ceremony, spanning multiple award categories.

	ACFM’s most recent edition, its 20th in 2025, pulled in 1,222 companies and 3,024 professionals from 55 countries for what became its biggest turnout yet, with on-site attendance hitting 30,006. Deals struck through its sales market totaled 8,438 business meetings and an estimated $71.1 million in transactions.

	The 21st ACFM runs Oct. 10-13 within the wider 31st Busan International Film Festival, which spans Oct. 6-15.

title: Robin Williams’ Daughter Calls for Fans Creating AI Videos of the Actor to ‘Have Some Shame’: ‘Leave Him Out of Your Delusional Bulls—’
description: Zelda Williams is calling for fans to stop circulating AI-generated videos of her late father, Robin Williams, nearly a year after she last took to
body:
Zelda Williams is calling for fans to stop circulating AI-generated videos of her late father, Robin Williams, nearly a year after she last took to social media to ask them not to send her augmented content featuring the actor.

	In a statement posted to X on Monday, the “Lisa Frankenstein” director wrote that a “supposedly ‘private video’” circulating of her father “is clearly AI, and not even particularly convincing AI,” she wrote. “Anyone who claims to be a fan who believes it clearly listened to his movies on mute because that voice is robotic and terrible. That said, a human made a robot create it, and to you I say: leave him out of your delusional bullshit and let him rest. If you cannot make your case without making a dead man make it more convincing for you, then tell me: who’s the one manipulating the public thru media now?”
	

	Zelda continued: “I hate this cesspool of an app. It’s mostly bots and people willingly being duped by bots at this point so not sure why I feel the need to come back to clarify, but I love him, so I will. Just because he’s gone does not mean he’s now your puppet. Have some shame.”


	The iconic comedian, who starred in films including “Jumanji,” “Good Will Hunting,” “Dead Poets Society,” “Hook,” “Mrs. Doubtfire,” and more, died in 2014 at the age of 63. In recent years, his likeness has become a popular target for AI recreation as users continue to create and share augmented videos of the actor.

	This isn’t the first time Zelda has voiced her feelings about AI; Back in Oct. 2025, she wrote “Please, just stop sending me AI videos of Dad” on Instagram. “Stop believing I wanna see it or that I’ll understand, I don’t and I won’t. If you’re just trying to troll me, I’ve seen way worse, I’ll restrict and move on. But please, if you’ve got any decency, just stop doing this to him and to me, to everyone even, full stop. It’s dumb, it’s a waste of time and energy, and believe me, it’s NOT what he’d want.”
	

	Just last month, she revived her father’s Instagram account with siblings Zak and Cody in an attempt to “fight back against rampant AI abuse of his voice and likeness on here.”

That supposedly ‘private video’ of dad that I’ve been shown talking about conspiracies is clearly AI, and not even particularly convincing AI. Anyone who claims to be a fan who believes it clearly listened to his movies on mute because that voice is robotic and terrible. That…— Zelda Williams (@zeldawilliams) September 21, 2026

title: Tom Cruise Says AI Is ‘Coming and It’s Going to Happen,’ but ‘People Want to See Real Things’: ‘Keep Creating’
description:
Despite the threat of AI to the film industry, Tom Cruise is confident that people will always “want to see real things” on screen.

	At an intimate
body:
Despite the threat of AI to the film industry, Tom Cruise is confident that people will always “want to see real things” on screen.

	At an intimate BAFTA “Life in Pictures” conversation in London on Monday night, Cruise looked back on his four-decade career including acclaimed roles in “Top Gun,” “Jerry Maguire,” “Magnolia” and the “Mission: Impossible” franchise as well as to the future with his upcoming movie “Digger.” 


	On the topic of how the “Mission: Impossible” films have been at the forefront of new technology — with 2025’s “The Final Reckoning” even taking on AI as its villain — moderator Edith Bowman asked Cruise for his take on how it will impact the industry. 
	

	“Here’s the thing: There is nothing like human,” Cruise began, explaining that one of the reasons he is so bullish on keeping the theatrical experience alive is because it brings people together. 

	“I have nothing against streaming or anything like that,” he continued, saying that seeing a film in theaters is simply “a different art form.”

	He pointed to this summer’s box office — which broke all-time industry records by grossing $4.76 billion from May 1 to Labor Day — as an example of the enduring desire for human stories and craftsmanship.

	“People want that experience. They’re going to movie theaters,” Cruise said, adding: “I always believe in humanity.”

	Cruise concluded that in the face of AI, creatives must “keep creating.” 

	“You know, it is coming and it’s going to happen,” Cruise said of AI. “But people want to see real things.”

	The movie star also teased “Digger,” directed by “The Revenant” helmer Alejandro G. Iñárritu, in which he plays a wealthy oil tycoon. Cruise looks nearly unrecognizable in the role, sporting a fat suit and prosthetics he said initially took six hours to apply. 
	

	“I’ve never read a movie like this,” Cruise said. “It’s the most original film and one of the most moving films I’ve ever seen.”

	“Digger” hits theaters on Oct. 2 via Warner Bros.

title: Netflix Partners With British Library, Sets Talks Series With Florence Pugh, Zoe Kazan and More
description: Netflix has teamed with one of the most famous cultural institutions in the U.K., the British Library, to help “more people discover the books behin
body:
Netflix has teamed with one of the most famous cultural institutions in the U.K., the British Library, to help “more people discover the books behind some of the world’s most popular films and series,” it says.

	The new national partnership, which will include local libraries across the U.K., comes as 2026 marks the National Year of Reading, an initiative aimed at reversing the sharp decline in reading for pleasure across the U.K.


	Alongside dedicated funding from Netflix to support the British Library’s literary conservation and archives, this new partnership will see collections of books that have been adapted into Netflix films and series donated to 100 public libraries across the U.K. The collections will include titles including “Frankenstein,” “Pride and Prejudice”, “Heartstopper,” “One Day,” “The Thursday Murder Club” and “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.”
	

	In addition to the donated collections, Netflix and the British Library will host a programme of events also streamed to libraries across the country about how books are brought to the screen. The programme has already included Q&As with the stars of “Frankenstein,” “The Thursday Murder Club”, and “The Seven Dials Mystery.” On Monday night, Florence Pugh, Zoe Kazan, Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist discussed the making of “East of Eden.”

	“Every great adaptation starts with a great story. We are proud to bring these stories to audiences all over the world, but we also know the experience does not have to end when the credits roll,” said Anne Mensah, Vice President of Content, U.K. at Netflix.
	

	“Books and screen adaptations can introduce audiences to different worlds, ideas and voices. Through our partnership with the British Library, we hope to help more people discover the books behind the shows and films they love, while supporting the public libraries that make reading accessible to communities across the country.”

	The U.K. National Literacy Trust’s 2025 Annual Literacy Survey found that children’s enjoyment of reading had fallen to its lowest recorded level. Howvever, it also showed that books linked to favourite films and TV series can encourage reluctant readers. The same is true for adults, with Nielsen BookData finding that 12% of adult fiction bought by occasional readers was discovered through, or chosen because of, a film or television adaptation.

	‘’We are delighted to be partnering with Netflix. With this partnership we’re helping to bring Netflix’s exciting literary adaptations to new audiences across the U.K. via our Living Knowledge Network of public libraries,” Helen Schulte, the British Library’s head of culture programmes. “We’re so grateful to Netflix for partnering with the Library and providing much needed philanthropic support for conservation, helping to preserve the treasures we care for as the U.K.’s national library.”

title: Christina Applegate Shares First Video Following Months-Long Hospitalization: ‘Love to You All Out There’
description: Christina Applegate has shared a first look at her life outside the hospital following a months-long stay amid her ongoing battle with multiple scle
body:
Christina Applegate has shared a first look at her life outside the hospital following a months-long stay amid her ongoing battle with multiple sclerosis.

	In the video, shared on Applegate’s Instagram account, the “Married… with Children” star is seen showing off her blonde hair while wearing a black zip-up hoodie. “Fresh hair color, new weird spot on my cheek haha thank you @davestanwell for brightening up my cloudy day,” Applegate wrote.
	

	The Emmy winner also shouted out those who have been supporting her: “Love you and love to you all out there,” she wrote.


	News first broke that Applegate had been hospitalized back in March, though the next month, she took to Instagram to share that she’d been “getting stronger and better every day.”

	“Thank you for the outpouring of love and well wishes,” she wrote in her caption on Monday. “Health issues are a constant for me, but I’m a strong chick and I’m getting stronger and better every day. I’m taking a moment to focus on my health, but I’ll be back with more to say soon enough.”

	Applegate first announced her MS diagnosis in Aug. 2021, and made her first public appearance when she attended her Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony the following year.

	When she took the stage during the ceremony, the “Dead to Me” actor began to cry when talking about her daughter.

	“The most important person in this world is my daughter,” Applegate said. “You are so much more than even you know. You are so beautiful and kind and smart and interesting. I’m blessed every day that I get to wake up and take you to school…thank you for standing by me through all of this.”
	

	Speaking to the audience, Applegate added, “Every single one of you. I love you [all] so much.”

schema.headline: Christina Applegate Shares First Video Following Months-Long Hospitalization: ‘Love to You All Out There’

title: Paramount-Warner Bros. Settlement: What the Guilds, AGs and Activists Are Saying
description: After almost a year in the trenches pulling together his historic combination of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison has fi
body:
After almost a year in the trenches pulling together his historic combination of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison has finally emerged victorious. On Monday, the Silicon Valley heir confirmed he’d reached a settlement with a group of state attorneys general, who sued to block the merger over antitrust concerns. 

	The proposed merger was met with heated opposition by activist groups, top talent like Mark Ruffalo and  whispers by Ellison’s legacy media competitors. But groups like the Hollywood labor guilds are celebrating the settlement news, as the staring contest between Ellison and the AGs caused paralysis in development and spending seemingly across the board at both companies.
	

	Here are the cheers, jeers and looming fears of the players involved in “ParaBros”: WGAThe outspoken union acknowledged that their own active litigation against the ParaBros. merger could no longer continue once the state AG’s settled, largely over the cost of duking it out in court.


	“We continue to believe the merger will cause damage to writers and the industry at large. Now that the Attorneys General have settled with Paramount, however, as a nonprofit, the WGA must contend with the reality of forging ahead alone, with no backing from government enforcers, with a complex antitrust lawsuit that would cost millions of dollars to pursue through trial. Consequently, we have also settled our lawsuit with an agreement from Paramount to prohibit writer layoffs at CBS News Broadcast for 5 years, and to pay $17.5 million to our health fund along with our attorneys’ fees in the litigation. Though we were not successful in blocking the merger, our advocacy brought more attention to the harms that this merger—and others like it—will cause. We will continue to fight the harms of industry consolidation.

	As the number of outlets to sell our work to and the corresponding diversity of programming shrinks, we need industry-wide structural separation between streamers and studios in order to promote competition in programming, like the Financial Interest and Syndication Rules once required in broadcast television. We will continue to fight for these goals.”
	

	DGAThe Directors Guild of America highlighted protections that the AG’s negotiated (read a comprehensive list of those here). 

	“We congratulate the parties on reaching an agreement that addresses a number of critical concerns related to the Paramount/WBD merger. The AG agreement contains important binding and enforceable commitments that protect theatrical film and television markets and domestic film jobs. Equally important, it brings clarity and stability to the industry during a period of decreased production. We especially thank California Attorney General Rob Bonta, and New York Attorney General Letitia James, for their leadership. We intend to continue our discussions with Paramount regarding domestic television production, with a focus on ensuring a competitive and robust marketplace that protects jobs.”

	SAG-AFTRAThe actors union underscored the power of collective bargaining. 

	“The settlement of the Attorneys General antitrust lawsuit, announced today, addresses some of our deep concerns about production levels and investment in U.S. production… We will continue to approach our relationship with Paramount with professionalism and the intention to work well together. We hope that the process of engaging with the attorneys general has impressed upon them the fact that in addition to collective bargaining, our members rely on the law to help protect our interests. These are the lowest standards that our employers must meet. All of the companies have the opportunity to exceed their legal obligations and make additional efforts to ensure that our workplaces are healthy and that employers honor our dignity.”

	Mark Ruffalo“Task” star Ruffalo is the face of celebrity dissent over the merger, engaging in an ugly back-and-forth with Paramount after promoting what the studio called “antisemitic tropes.”  

	“Gavin Newsom hands huge win to Trump and his billionaire cronies,” Ruffalo wrote simply on X, referring to California Governor Newsom.California Attorney General Rob BontaIf Ruffalo is the face of celebrity dissent, then Bonta was the final boss. Ellison’s most vocal opponent said this about his own settlement deal on Monday: 

	”Today, we have secured a settlement that resolves our antitrust concerns of the Warner Bros./Paramount merger — concerns that the merger will lower output and increase prices — by guaranteeing massive investment in domestic film production and providing enforceable guardrails to help keep cable prices competitive. Let me be clear: This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger. But we believe this settlement, which resolves our antitrust concerns in every market alleged in our case, protects competition and consumer choice, and puts workers’ needs, concerns, and futures first, is the best course of action. When we get down to brass tacks, what we heard over and over from people who would be most directly and immediately impacted by the merger is that what matters most is consistent film output, domestic production, and protecting the livelihoods of workers above and below the line. As such, our settlement provides court-enforceable commitments for more films, an infusion of an additional $1.5 billion into home-grown film production, and protections for workers who are impacted by the merger. There’s no Hollywood without the people who work on and off screen to make the magic happen, and today’s settlement protects workers, jobs, and Hollywood.”Block the Merger Coalition The advocacy group formed this summer in response to the pending merger went, as predicted, scorched earth:“We vehemently oppose the agreement to allow David Ellison to take over Warner Bros. Discovery. This is a bad deal for the future of film, entertainment, independent journalism, and a strong democracy in this country. We are disappointed and angry that the interests of average Americans have been trampled to benefit oligarch billionaires.“The Ellisons and other forces arrayed against us, but that didn’t stop us and so many others from standing up. We are proud of what we accomplished, and together, our coalition will keep fighting. From the thousands of leaders in the film and entertainment industry and elected officials, to the hundreds of thousands who joined them to make their voices heard, even in the face of potential retaliation, this was a grassroots movement that proved Americans are not going to take this corruption anymore. That energy is not going away.“This isn’t the last we will hear of the Ellisons or the fallout of this merger – and it’s not the last you will hear from us. Block the Merger was never just about one merger, but about the harms of media consolidation and promoting a diversity of voices. We will continue fighting for accountability and policy reforms to break up and prevent these large conglomerates. This one battle may be over in our efforts to defend democracy, but we won’t stop fighting until we win the war.”

	More to come …

title: Rob Bonta, Facing Skeptics, Defends ‘Very Strong’ Paramount Deal
description: Rob Bonta defended the antitrust settlement that allows Paramount to merge with Warner Bros. on Monday, saying in a 45-minute press conference that
body:
Rob Bonta defended the antitrust settlement that allows Paramount to merge with Warner Bros. on Monday, saying in a 45-minute press conference that the deal includes independent monitoring and will result in more jobs in Hollywood.

	But the deal does not include the three words — robust structural remedies — that California’s attorney general had said was the goal since filing suit in July. And while he went to some lengths to argue that the deal represents a “strong” outcome, he also acknowledged it was not his preferred result.
	

	“I don’t think these two companies should merge,” he said. “But that’s not something that we are focused on with our resolution here.”


	Bonta had come under increasing pressure in the last few weeks, as Gov. Gavin Newsom, Xavier Becerra, the cinema trade group, and labor leaders all expressed hope for a settlement. Paramount also did its best to increase the leverage on Bonta, threatening to relocate to Tennessee and seeking a court order to force the 12-state coalition to pay $1.88 billion for delaying the deal.

	In the press conference, Bonta sought to downplay that pressure. “That’s not what I’m thinking about, that’s not my focus,” he said. making the case that the A.G.’s victories in court put pressure on Paramount to offer significant concessions.

	“We got the antitrust resolution that we wanted,” he said. “Very strong remedies and commitments to address the concerns that we raised.”

	As to whether he thought the states could have prevailed at trial next spring, he said that courtrooms “always have risk.” He also acknowledged concerns that prolonging the case would create “uncertainty” in Hollywood, an issue that had been raised by Paramount and some labor unions.
	

	“This deal gives certainty about the future of production right here in L.A.,” he said, noting that Paramount had committed to increasing domestic production and to not selling its L.A. lots for at least five years. “That also generates important certainty for this industry that I think is craving it.”

	He also argued that the outcome is dramatically different from the Hollywood’s last major merger, the Disney-Fox deal, which went unchallenged by antitrust authorities and led to reduced production.

	“This agreement is the opposite of Disney-Fox,” he said. “The things that we saw in the Disney-Fox merger — a massive decrease in film production… this doesn’t just guard against that and protect against the downside; it locks in a massive upside.”

	Bonta was alone at the podium, without his trial team or representatives from the other 11 states involved in the suit. He was also not joined by the Writers Guild of America, which filed its own antitrust suit and also resolved it over the weekend.

	In a statement, the WGA said that the settlement terms “fall far short of adequately protecting writers,” but that it could not bear the cost of continuing its suit without support from the states.

	William Tong, the attorney general of Connecticut, also expressed dismay that the deal does not include divesture of CBS and CNN, which he said was needed to save “ethical and independent journalism.”

	“We fought aggressively for that remedy,” he said. “I am deeply disappointed that we could not do more.”

	Bonta noted that all 12 states signed on to the settlement. He also said the WGA was not involved in the states’ negotiations.

	“They brought their own case,” he said. “They decided whether or not they wanted to resolve their case and under what terms.”

	Bonta said there was no key moment or provision that unlocked the deal, and struggled to offer a timeline of how the agreement came together.

	“These days have blurred because we’ve been in some deep and robust conversations,” he said.

schema.headline: Rob Bonta, Facing Skeptics, Defends ‘Very Strong’ Paramount Deal

title: ‘Daredevil: Born Again’ Ending With Season 3
description:
Daredevil is hanging up his mask after three seasons on Disney+.

	Marvel’s “Daredevil: Born Again,” starring Charlie Cox as the blind lawyer-turned
body:
Daredevil is hanging up his mask after three seasons on Disney+.

	Marvel’s “Daredevil: Born Again,” starring Charlie Cox as the blind lawyer-turned-vigilante, is ending with the upcoming Season 3, Variety has confirmed. The third and final season wrapped production a couple of months ago and is expected to premiere on Disney+ in 2027. Co-creator and showrunner Dario Scardapane has also exited the series, which is in the midst of post-production.
	

	Cox originally debuted as the blind hero on Netflix’s “Daredevil,” which ran for three seasons from 2015-2018 and kicked off the mini, street-level Marvel universe on the streamer. It spawned “Jessica Jones”, “Luke Cage” and “Iron Fist” spinoffs and culminated with the team-up series “The Defenders.” Disney+ revived the show as “Daredevil: Born Again” in 2025 and brought back several of the main cast members, including Vincent D’Onofrio as Wilson Fisk, aka the Kingpin of New York City, Deborah Ann Woll as Karen Page, Elden Henson as Foggy Nelson and Wilson Bethel as Bullseye.


	“Born Again” Season 2 started reuniting Netflix’s “Defenders” cast by bringing back Krysten Ritter as the super-strong private detective Jessica Jones in a supporting role, plus Mike Colter had a cameo in the finale as her lover Luke Cage. Paparazzi photos also leaked during Season 3 production, showing Finn Jones back as Danny Rand, aka the martial arts expert Iron Fist, alongside Ritter and Colter. They’re expected to team up once again to take down Kingpin, who’s been stripped of his title as New York City mayor. Meanwhile, Daredevil has found himself in jail, and his identity was made public in the wake of the Season 2 finale.
	

	Hollywood Reporter first reported the news of the series ending.

title: WGA Settles Antitrust Lawsuit With Paramount Over Warner Bros. Discovery Merger
description: The Writers Guild of America East and Writers Guild of America West, jointly the WGA, have settled their lawsuit to block the proposed merger of Par
body:
The Writers Guild of America East and Writers Guild of America West, jointly the WGA, have settled their lawsuit to block the proposed merger of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery per a statement released by the organization Monday.

	The settlement comes following the news that Paramount has reached a deal with 12 state attorneys general, removing a major obstacle to closing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.


	“We continue to believe the merger will cause damage to writers and the industry at large. Now that the Attorneys General have settled with Paramount, however, as a nonprofit, the WGA must contend with the reality of forging ahead alone, with no backing from government enforcers, with a complex antitrust lawsuit that would cost millions of dollars to pursue through trial,” reads the statement.
	

	The WGA also noted that while they “were not successful in blocking the merger,” the organization’s “advocacy brought more attention to the harms that this merger—and others like it—will cause. We will continue to fight the harms of industry consolidation.”

	The WGA filed the lawsuit to block the proposed $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance back in July. At the time, the organization alleged it would violate federal antitrust law and would cause specific harm to writers.

	“With fewer competitors, the merged Paramount-Warner Bros. entity would have both the incentive and the ability to lower costs by suppressing writers’ wages and reducing output. Writers will be paid less and have fewer employment opportunities,” the WGA complaint stated.
	

	The WGA’s lawsuit was filed following a prior antitrust lawsuit by 12 Democratic state attorneys that same month, which similarly alleged that the merger would give Paramount-WBD anticompetitive power in theatrical and basic cable TV markets.

	Read the WGA’s full statement here:

	“We continue to believe the merger will cause damage to writers and the industry at large. Now that the Attorneys General have settled with Paramount, however, as a nonprofit, the WGA must contend with the reality of forging ahead alone, with no backing from government enforcers, with a complex antitrust lawsuit that would cost millions of dollars to pursue through trial. Consequently, we have also settled our lawsuit with an agreement from Paramount to prohibit writer layoffs at CBS News Broadcast for 5 years, and to pay $17.5 million to our health fund along with our attorneys’ fees in the litigation.

	Though we were not successful in blocking the merger, our advocacy brought more attention to the harms that this merger—and others like it—will cause. We will continue to fight the harms of industry consolidation.

	As the number of outlets to sell our work to and the corresponding diversity of programming shrinks, we need industry-wide structural separation between streamers and studios in order to promote competition in programming, like the Financial Interest and Syndication Rules once required in broadcast television. We will continue to fight for these goals.”

title: David Ellison Says Paramount Hopes to Close Warner Bros. Deal in ‘Approximately Two Weeks’; Studios to Remain in California
description: Update: David Ellison isn’t looking for greener pastures. The CEO of Paramount Skydance (soon to include Warner Bros. Discovery) issued an official
body:
Update: David Ellison isn’t looking for greener pastures. The CEO of Paramount Skydance (soon to include Warner Bros. Discovery) issued an official statement that both content studios will remain in California. 

	“Now that we reached and announced a settlement, we’re eager to get to work building a stronger Hollywood. Let me be clear: the newly merged company will be headquartered in Los Angeles,” Ellison said hours after reaching a settlement with 12 state attorneys general and the WGA to clear a path for his merger.
	

	“We aren’t going anywhere. Our history is here and this is where our future is being built,” concluded Ellison. 


	Previously … 

	David Ellison’s endgame is in sight. Following a dramatic weekend of negotiations with a collection of state attorneys general and the WGA, the mogul’s path to combining Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is now clear.

	In a Monday address to staff, Ellison said his team’s goal is to “close in approximately two weeks. That said, closing is really just the starting line. Bringing two companies this size together takes time, and we’ll share information as it becomes available.”

	The mood is celebratory on the Paramount lot, insiders said, despite the fact that much of Hollywood is observing Yom Kippur (the most reverent of the Jewish High Holy Days). One source joked that several of Ellison’s top lieutenants will be making “guilt donations” to select charities for working through the day.

	While brief, the memo focused on the combined power that “ParaBros” will now wield to provide jobs and increase content volume (a stark narrative shift from the previously opposed group of AGs, who said the merger would be anticompetitive).
	

	“This is an exciting moment for our company and our industry. If you’re like me, you’re in this business because you love the art of visual storytelling – the chance to entertain, unite and inspire the world through extraordinary stories,” added Ellison. “Together, Paramount and WBD can do more of that, for audiences everywhere. And we can’t wait to get started.” 

	Read Ellison’s full memo to staff: 

	Team,Just a few moments ago, California Attorney General Rob Bonta, on behalf of himself and 11 other State AGs, announced a settlement that clears the path forward on the lawsuit blocking our merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. We have also reached a settlement with the Writers Guild of America.With both groups’ concerns now addressed, we have complete clearance for this merger and can move toward closing. There’s still work ahead to get this deal across the finish line, but we’re excited to bring these two iconic companies together, as it means more opportunity for our creatives, production crews and employees across the business, and more great entertainment for audiences everywhere.We’re grateful to Attorney General Bonta and his fellow AGs, and to the WGA, for engaging in good faith to reach this resolution. The agreement includes a number of commitments, including 30+ films annually and expanded U.S. film production – meant to help revitalize our industry and support the people behind it, here at home. Since we launched this bid, our goal has been to build a stronger Hollywood: more stories told, greater choice for consumers, stronger competition. Combining these companies gives us the opportunity to do just that.This is an exciting moment for our company and our industry. If you’re like me, you’re in this business because you love the art of visual storytelling – the chance to entertain, unite and inspire the world through extraordinary stories. Together, Paramount and WBD can do more of that, for audiences everywhere. And we can’t wait to get started.I know you have questions about what happens next – your role, your team and how we will work day to day. We don’t have all the answers yet, and I won’t pretend otherwise. We are tentatively planning to close in approximately two weeks. That said, closing is really just the starting line. Bringing two companies this size together takes time, and we’ll share information as it becomes available. In the meantime, if you have questions or concerns, please visit the Integration Hub, reach out to your manager or HR representative, or email internalcomms@paramount.com.Thank you for your patience, commitment and hard work throughout this process. I know it’s created real uncertainty, and for some of you, real anxiety – that’s not lost on me. Our people are what make this company one of the best in the world, and I’m truly grateful for your dedication and support. I’m confident we’re going to build something special together in the years ahead.Let’s go!David

schema.headline: David Ellison Says Paramount Hopes to Close Warner Bros. Deal in ‘Approximately Two Weeks’; Studios to Remain in California

title: Detroit Woman Discovers Mother Not in Casket, Cremated Weeks Before
description:
Detroit, Michigan
                          That's Not My Mom
                          ... Woman
body:
Detroit, Michigan
                          That's Not My Mom
                          ... Woman Shocked to Find Stranger in Casket
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 21, 2026
                            6:13 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Detroit woman is demanding answers after her mother's casket was opened and another woman was lying inside it -- because someone had apparently created her own mom.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... Kimberley Moore recently passed away in Michigan, and her family -- including her daughter Bianca -- was handling funeral arrangements according to detailed instructions Kimberley left behind.
      
    
            During the process, Bianca went to the Hutchinson Funeral Home in Detroit to see her body before the official viewing ... and she realized the person in the casket wasn't her mom -- though it wasn't her face that tipped her off, she said.
      

            Bianca told Fox 10 News in Detroit ... "I looked at her feet, and I didn’t see that mole that my mom has on her feet, and I looked at that man and I said, 'Sir, this is not my mama,' and he said it just like this. He said, ‘I’m sorry. They must have cremated your mom a week or two ago. I’m so sorry.'"
      
    
            She says she and her family are trying to figure out where her mother's ashes might be now ... and she also wants the body to be identified, so the other woman's actual family can pay their respects.
      
    
            Hutchinson Funeral Home shared a statement regarding the mix-up: “We are heartbroken and deeply sorry for what Ms. Moore’s family has experienced. We have launched our own internal review to determine exactly what happened, and we will deal with it accordingly.”
      
    
            Everybody makes mistakes ... but that's not going to bring Kimberley's family much comfort.

title: Clavicular Charged With Rape in Massachusetts, Influencer's Rep Fires Back
description:
Clavicular
                          Charged With Rape, Drugging Woman For Sex
body:
Clavicular
                          Charged With Rape, Drugging Woman For Sex
                          Influencer's Rep Fires Back
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 21, 2026
                            7:33 PM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Clavicular is facing serious charges, including one count of rape, in Massachusetts ... and it appears to be in connection with similar allegations made by a woman who is suing him in civil court.
      
    
            The Bulwark released a report on Monday ... stating Clav has been charged with rape, drugging a person for sex, and providing alcohol to a minor, all related to an alleged incident that went down in May 2025.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            While the alleged victim in the case has not been identified, it appears to be the same incident relayed by influencer Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza in a civil lawsuit she filed earlier this year.
      

            A rep for Clavicular tells TMZ, "She filed a lawsuit and doesn’t include sexual assault as a count. She then amends it and adds it a couple of months later."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The rep said Clav is fighting the civil lawsuit and believes the influencer has evidence to refute her claims.
      
    
            His rep added, "She and her lawyer then go to police."
      
    
            Sources close to Clav believe the entire situation is a shakedown and they "will be fighting this till the end."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Aleksandra alleges Clavicular paid her $1,000 to film videos for him in May 2025 when she was 16 and said he wanted her to be the female face for "looksmaxxing."
      
    
            Mendoza alleged in her civil suit that she met Clav at a house in Cape Cod, Mass., where excessive amounts of alcohol were served, and that she became very intoxicated. She says while she was drunk, Clav had sex with her despite the fact that she was unable to give consent, and then claims she woke up the next morning to him having sex with her again without her consent. The age of legal consent in Massachusetts is 16, so Clavicular is not facing any child sex charges.
      
    
            Clavicular's attorney Steve Kramer told us at the time the civil case was filed ... "We are aware of the complaint recently filed against Mr. Peters [Clavicular]. These are allegations only and remain unproven. Mr. Peters denies the claims and disputes the characterization of events. He will respond through the appropriate legal channels and intends to vigorously defend himself. We will not comment further at this time."

                          Seemingly Wasn't Sober When He Entered Rehab
body:
Presley Gerber
                          Seemingly Wasn't Sober When He Entered Rehab
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 21, 2026
                            7:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Presley Gerber appeared under the influence of a substance when he checked into the luxury rehab home where he would later die ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources who had contact with Presley in his final hours tell TMZ he did not appear sober when he arrived at the Santa Monica facility Saturday night, while seeking help for substance abuse issues.
      
    
            As we first reported ... the 27-year-old model was found unresponsive at the home Sunday morning and cops responded to a suspected overdose call around 9:35 AM.
      

            A spokesperson for the Santa Monica Police Department told us officers located an unresponsive individual at the facility and performed life-saving measures. Presley was pronounced dead approximately 10 minutes later.
      
    
            His death is being investigated as a suspected drug overdose. No foul play is suspected, and an official cause of death has yet to be released.
      
    
            Presley's family -- supermodel Cindy Crawford, businessman Rande Gerber and actress and model Kaia Gerber -- has asked for privacy as they grieve.

title: 'That's So Raven' Kyle Massey Offers Support to Bobb'e J. Thompson After Prison Sentence
description:
'That's So Raven' Star Kyle Massey
                          We Still Love You, Bobb'e J. ...
body:
'That's So Raven' Star Kyle Massey
                          We Still Love You, Bobb'e J. ...
                          Let Me Know if You Need Anything In Prison
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 21, 2026
                            5:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Bobb'e J. Thompson's headed to prison for a couple years ... but he won't be abandoned by his longtime friends on the outside ... 'cause Kyle Massey says he's got the dude's back.
      
    
            We caught up with Kyle -- who starred with Bobb'e J. on the beloved Disney Channel show "That's So Raven" -- at LAX on Monday ... and our photog asked about Bobby recently being sentenced to 30 months in federal prison.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kyle immediately sends love to Bobb'e ... adding "Free Bobb'e J" and calling him his brother. He says he and others support Bobb'e, and they're always going to have his back.
      

            He says Bobb'e was always laser-focused on his acting and his comedy ... and he didn't notice anything going on with him prior to his federal gun case.
      
    
            As we reported ... Bobb'e was sentenced to hard time after he was arrested in 2025 during a routine traffic stop -- when cops say they found a stolen firearm in his car. Bobb'e pled guilty back in April, but the sentence didn't come down until last week.
      
    
            Bobb'e was also reportedly convicted of battery causing serious bodily injury, assault, and prohibited firearm possession in 2022 ... but clearly he's still got friends in Hollywood.
